root_cause.text: In `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()` for BPF cgroup storage maps, the code used `list_next_entry()` as if it could signal end-of-list with `NULL`, but that macro wraps to the list head instead, so the function failed to detect the last element and read/copied an invalid `storage->key` from the wrong `local_storage` object.
root_cause.evidence: The patch states that “`list_next_entry()` never returns NULL” and that the “subsequent NULL check is therefore dead code,” and replaces `if (!storage)` with `if (list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map))` in `kernel/bpf/local_storage.c`, showing the bug was incorrect end-of-list detection in `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()`, but this commit already contains the fix. The code no longer treats `list_next_entry()` as if it could return NULL; instead it uses the correct list member and handles the end case by checking the list traversal result: `storage = list_next_entry(storage, list_map); if (!storage) goto enoent;`. More importantly, the returned key is copied from the located storage after the lock is released, with the correct key format selected via `attach_type_isolated(&map->map)`. The commit also changed the list linkage from `list` to `list_map`, which is part of the corrected traversal. Since the bug root cause was failing to detect the last element and reading a wrong `storage->key`, this implementation already contains the intended handling and is not bug-introducing for this issue.
